description: One entry per measured conformance run, oldest first. runs[0] is the baseline the compatibility report compares against. Written by conformance/report/build-report.mjs; an entry is keyed by label + generatedAt, so rebuilding the report from the same results file updates that entry and leaves the rest of the trend intact. `flags` records the runner flags the numbers were measured with: a run without --reload-per-spec is not comparable to one with it.

runs.label: baseline
runs.note: Baseline named in the acceleration plan: 135 passed, 1018 failed, 1153 ran of 1539 extracted. Runner flags were not recorded and this run predates --reload-per-spec; its 257 skips also predate the needs-config status, so 124 cases now reported needs-config were skips here.

runs.label: wave work, no relationship manifest
runs.note: Same tree as the run below, with PGREST_RELATIONSHIPS_PATH unset: the engine has no relationship source at all on DSQL. Kept in the trend to show what that one setting is worth.

runs.label: wave work, relationship manifest configured
runs.note: Published run. Engine changes are uncommitted on top of 3fbf941, which is also the baseline commit.

runs.label: verified, per-spec reload
runs.note: Independently re-run and verified; 550/1199. id-matched vs baseline: +422 pass, -7 regress.

runs.label: verified, no per-spec reload
runs.note: Controlled run to isolate the value of --reload-per-spec: 443 vs 550 on identical code.

runs.label: eeb1ac9 implementation run
runs.note: The implementing pass's own full-suite run of this tree. Kept in the trend for comparison with the verification re-run of the same tree 27 minutes later; the published headline is the verification run, not this one.

runs.label: eeb1ac9 verification re-run
runs.note: Independent full-suite re-run by the verification pass on the same tree as the implementation run at 21:28 (943/1285); published in preference to it because it was measured by the checker rather than the author. Same flags as the 550/1199 run, so that comparison is flag-matched.

runs.label: eeb1ac9 independent re-measurement
runs.note: Third full run on the same tree, measured by the orchestrator rather than by an implementing or verifying agent. Same-tree runs measured 943, 945 and 948 passing; this is the middle one and it is published in preference to the highest. The runner's base engine config sets bulkMutationGuard off, faithful to upstream's baseCfg (upstream loads pg-safeupdate only inside PgSafeUpdateSpec, per test/spec/Main.hs), and applies per-case config for the settings upstream sets with withConfig; that is worth roughly a dozen cases and is not visible in the flags string. All five cases that regressed against the 550/1199 run are measurement artifacts: four are row-order-unspecified order luck, and UpsertSpec:417 passes under --reset-touched, confirming residual within-spec fixture pollution rather than an engine regression.

runs.label: acd3b91 post-merge
runs.note: Full suite on the merge commit, before the ceiling wave. Verified the origin/main merge (Cedar per-row insert authorization, SSM passwords) cost no passing checks: 941/1285 against the published 945/1285, 4 gained and 8 lost, of which 7 are row-order-unspecified and 1 (InsertSpec:596) was a row left in simple_pk2 by an earlier run — a table 03-schema.sql creates and 07-data.sql never populates, so no reset cleared it. That hole is closed in this wave.

runs.label: integration
runs.note: Implementation pass's own full-suite run of this tree: 1066/1358, the lowest of the four. Not published, per the rule against publishing the run measured by the pass that wrote the code. Wave: fixture sequence rewind, declared data representations, 11 more upstream process settings booted, 42703 for unknown columns, RPC 416 fix. Two corrections to this entry made at publish time: the flags string is back to the canonical one (it had been widened with 'PGREST_REPRESENTATIONS_PATH defaulted', which silently dropped the run out of every flag-matched comparison; the runner defaults that variable for --target dsql in every run here, so it is not a flag difference), and tree records the integration commit 5586e94 because the run was measured on the working tree before that commit existed, so its own commit field reads acd3b91.

runs.label: 5586e94 2026-08-21T10:46:24Z
runs.note: Audit pass, first of its three full-suite runs of this tree: 1073/1358, tied highest. Not published, per the rule preferring the middle of the observed range to the top. Provenance: found in the audit pass's output directory; the audit's report quoted only its last run. A results file does not record its flags, so they are recorded here as the canonical string on the evidence that this run's 1,539-case set and its blocked / needs-config / skipped / out-of-scope counts (129 / 2 / 35 / 15) match the published run exactly. Against the published run it passes 12 cases that run failed (10 order-unspecified assertions plus RpcSpec:985 and RpcSpec:997, whose failure text is also an ordering difference) and fails 8 it passed (6 UpsertSpec cases that depend on identity-sequence state a data-only fixture reload does not restore, plus 2 more order-unspecified assertions).

runs.label: 5586e94 2026-08-21T10:54:57Z
runs.note: Audit pass, second of its three full-suite runs of this tree: 1073/1358, tied highest. Not published, same reason, same provenance caveat as the 10:46:24Z run. It differs from the run 8 minutes before it on 16 cases and from the published run on 6, and every one of those is an order-unspecified assertion or one of the six sequence-dependent UpsertSpec cases: two runs can agree on the total and disagree on which cases passed, which is what run-to-run noise looks like.

runs.label: 5586e94 2026-08-21T11:09:15Z
runs.note: PUBLISHED. Third and last full-suite run measured by the independent audit pass: 1069/1358 (78.7%). Chosen over the implementation pass's own 1066 run (never publish the run measured by the pass that wrote the code) and over the two 1073 runs (prefer the middle of the observed range to the top). This wave: fixture sequence rewind, declared data representations for a database that rejects CREATE CAST, 11 more upstream process settings booted by the harness, PostgreSQL's own 42703 for an unknown column in place of PGRST204, RPC 416 fix, mutation payload and Prefer handling, protocol headers and Vary, media-type negotiation, embed depth and disambiguation.

runs.label: 68b09a4 2026-08-21T11:54:33Z
runs.note: Independent replication of the published tree, run from a clean checkout of 68b09a4 one minute after that commit: 1067/1358. Lowest of the four measurements of this tree, which widens the observed range to 1067-1073 and leaves the published 1069 near its middle. Every case it disagrees with the published run about is row-order-unspecified — it loses EmbedDisambiguationSpec:278, QuerySpec:571 and QuerySpec:1313 and gains JsonOperatorSpec:248 — so the run-to-run spread on this tree is order luck on a handful of cases and nothing structural. Recorded rather than discarded because a replication that comes out below the published number is exactly the one worth keeping.
